description: Save a chatbot test on a saved connector (`connectorId`, from listDigitalConnectors or createDigitalConnector): what the customer wants (`mission`), what counts as success (`acceptance`) and, optionally, the exact messages to send in order (`probes`). Saves the test and sends nothing; run it with runDigitalTest. If a required value was not given (the phone number, what should be heard, what counts as success), ask for it; do not invent one. Say which optional settings are being left at their defaults. Use when: what a chatbot does in a conversation is to be checked.

connectorId.description:
The connector this test runs against. Resolved at LAUNCH time, so
editing a connector updates every test pointing at it.

profile.description: Test data a `standard` run's steps draw on. The voice profile shape minus `voiceItems`.

profileId.description:
Reference to a saved profile (see `/profiles`) to draw test data from —
the same mechanism voice tests use. Resolved at RUN time, so editing the
profile updates every test that points at it rather than leaving stale
copies behind. Takes precedence over an inline `profile`.

A profile that resolves to no usable items is rejected with 400 rather
than run with no data — a test that silently sent nothing would fail
against a perfectly good bot and read as a product defect.

samples.description: Defaults to 3 for the judged kinds and 1 for `standard`.

items.description:
One step of a `kind: standard` test, discriminated on `type`.

Modelled as a discriminated union rather than one permissive object so a
generated client cannot build a step that the API will reject - an `expect`
with no `expected`, for instance.

allOf.description:
Send a customer message. Supply EXACTLY ONE of `text` or `profileItemId` -
both, or neither, is a 400.

`profileItemId` is a key into `profile.dataItems`, mirroring how a voice
DTMF step resolves one. There is no template syntax: an unresolvable
reference fails loudly rather than sending the literal `{{accountNumber}}`
to the bot.

Assert the bot's next message.

`exact` is the default because chat delivers the bytes the bot sent. Voice
has to fuzzy-match at a threshold because ASR is lossy; defaulting to one
here would silently pass near-misses. Matching trims and collapses
whitespace but is case-SENSITIVE - a bot that changed case changed its
output.

threshold.description: Only consulted by `similarity`, but reported on every result row so a failure shows the bar it was judged against.

allOf.description: Pause. For targets that rate-limit, or to let an async handoff settle.
Close the conversation explicitly. Optional - the runner closes the transport anyway.

name: createDigitalTestConfig

allOf.description:
The reusable parts of a digital test. `connectorId`/`target`/`targetRef` are
held here as the default but can be overridden at launch — running the same
test against a different bot is the common case.

Either `connectorId` or a complete `target`+`targetRef` pair is required.
`connectorId` is resolved into the concrete target at LAUNCH time, so
editing the connector updates every config that points at it; the inline
pair is TRANSITIONAL and accepted only until every config has been
backfilled with a connector.

Per-kind rules are enforced at SAVE time, not just at launch: a config that
could never run is rejected with 400 rather than stored for you to discover
later. This excludes whether a `connectorId` actually resolves — that is not
checked until LAUNCH, so a typo'd, deleted, or cross-workspace connector still
saves with 200 and only fails when a run is started, before any billing occurs.

Microsoft Bot Framework Direct Line 3.0: Copilot Studio agents and Azure Bot
Service bots. Holds a token endpoint URL, never a Direct Line secret.

directLineDomain.description:
The Direct Line host, for example `https://europe.directline.botframework.com`.
When absent it is discovered (Copilot Studio) or the global host is used.

skipStartEvent.description:
A `startConversation` event is sent when the conversation opens, which is what
makes a Copilot Studio agent greet. Set true for a bot that greets on its own.

target.description:
TRANSITIONAL — inline target. Superseded by `connectorId`; required
together with `targetRef` only when `connectorId` is absent.

targetRef.description:
TRANSITIONAL — inline target identity. Superseded by `connectorId`;
required together with `target` only when `connectorId` is absent.
